title: OpenProposal decision record
description: One decision per file: decisions/<id>.yaml. It quotes the IR elements it covers and stores their digests, so it goes stale when one of them changes. Mapping entries cite it as their source.

status.description: `proposed` until a human accepts it; `filed` once it is raised with the working group; `superseded` when a later record replaces it; `withdrawn` when its owner drops it and no record replaces it, so the reading it chose is no longer ours and nothing may cite it. A superseded or withdrawn record stays, unchanged but for its status and the `superseded_by` or `withdrawn` it gains, so its history is kept. A release fails on a `proposed` record.

kind.description: `gap`: the specification leaves the point open, and the decision chooses a reading. `departure`: the specification settles the point, in its text or in the form its examples write, and the decision proposes a change. An example that follows the specification but not a departure is a finding of the departure, and its reason says that the example follows the text.

author.description: Who proposed the decision: `agent`, or a person's name.

question.description: What the specification leaves open, as one question.

covers.description: The IR elements the decision rests on, each quoted and digested.

options.description: The alternatives considered, including the chosen one.

evidence.description: Further sources, such as an example file and line, or another specification.

feedback.description: What the specification should say instead, for the implementation feedback to the working group.

issue.description: Where the decision was filed. Required when `status` is `filed`.

superseded_by.description: The record that replaces this one. Required when `status` is `superseded`.

withdrawn.description: Why and when the record was withdrawn. Required when `status` is `withdrawn`, and only then.

sets_aside.description: The types the decision gives a field whose structure the specification doesn't state, such as an open vocabulary with no core terms, each with the field that holds it. The duplication and value-list gates set aside exactly these: a type of no structure that no record lists fails, and so does a listed type that is gone, has a structure, or isn't the field's.

field.description: The field or member that holds the type, as the specification writes its path, such as `reporting.delivery_mechanism`.

ir.description: The IR element that defines the type, which the record covers.

allOf.description: Only a departure lists, on a cover, the forms it departs from.
A withdrawn record says why and when, and no other record does.

digest.description: The element's digest when the record was written. A different current digest makes the record stale.

quote.description: The element's text as `npm run cite` prints it. The gate compares it with the IR, so a quote can't be edited by hand.

locks.description: Lock names the cover applies to. Without it, the cover applies to every lock.

departs.description: For a departure: the constraint forms of this element that it changes, as the fidelity gate reads them from the specification (`required`, `optional`, `conditional`, `type`, `values`, `contains`, `member`, `empty`, `example`, `default`). The gate lets the schema disagree with this element's constraint of a listed form, and with no other, and fails a listed form that excuses no disagreement on a lock the cover applies to, so a departure about one element's type excuses neither its presence nor another element it covers.
